value_domain: PLIDA synthetic person identifier (Agency Entity Unique ID)
value_source: Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine
variable_description: The patient a Medicare claim line belongs to, carried as a meaningless code so that one person's services can be followed across the date-of-service tables without a Medicare number. The Productivity Commission describes how the ABS builds it: "The ABS transforms unique identifiers in the original dataset into a Synthetic AEUID, enabling the datasets within PLIDA modules to be connected with one another, while preventing re-identification in the dataset outside of it". It is the only person-level key on the row, so grouping by it turns claim lines into a patient's service history, with BENPAID, FEECHARGED and NUMSERV summing per person and ITEM, BTOS and MBSCAT saying what was done. Different datasets from one data source carry consistent values, so the column joins the MBS tables to each other, but the Productivity Commission describes every dataset in the PLIDA Modular Product as joined through its own concordance table, so a join to PBS, AIR or any other dataset should be confirmed against those tables rather than assumed, and reaching Census, ATO or Centrelink data means going through the spine linkage file.
description_source: Productivity Commission, 'A-PLIDA-nalysis: Using PLIDA for public policy research and reporting', section on the Person Linkage Spine
value_definition: An opaque code standing in for the patient's Medicare enrolment identifier, repeated on every claim line for that person and held consistently across the tables from the same source. It follows no published classification and carries no age, sex, location or card information, so there is no finite list to publish and nothing in the value to decode or order.
limitation: The value cannot be matched against the identifier for the same person in another agency's data, because the Productivity Commission notes that "Synthetic AEUIDs are unique to an entity within a data source and are not repeated across sources": an MBS value equal to a Census or ATO value is a coincidence, not a person. It names the patient the service was for, not the person who lodged the claim or paid the account, and not the practitioner, who is SCRAM_SPR when servicing and SCRAM_RPR when referring. Whether the patient can be reached anywhere else in PLIDA depends on the separate spine linkage file, in which a record that did not match the spine carries no spine identifier at all.
rationale: The PLIDA data item list gives this field as the synthetic MADIP person ID on all 259 MBS date-of-service claims tables from 2006 to 2025, being 240 monthly tables and 19 annual supplementary tables, and the Productivity Commission's PLIDA guide documents what a Synthetic AEUID is, how the ABS creates it, that it is unique within one data source, and that concordance tables carry it to a Spine AEUID. The ABS names the column itself on its Labour Force Survey-PLIDA page, saying the survey's person identifier is replaced with an anonymised PLIDA person ID SYNTHETIC_AEUID, which confirms the same design applies column for column. That the MBS value is the patient rather than the provider comes from the columns beside it: SCRAM_SPR and SCRAM_RPR carry the providers, and the MBS note on ENRPC says the patient demographics on the row are sourced from the Medicare enrolment file at the time the claim was processed.
evidence_quote: The ABS transforms unique identifiers in the original dataset into a Synthetic AEUID, enabling the datasets within PLIDA modules to be connected with one another, while preventing re-identification in the dataset outside of it.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's four words, 'Synthetic MADIP Person ID', with a domain of 'Opaque identifier (inferred)' guessed from the variable name and a value definition and limitation that both said only that the domain was inferred from the name and open. Nothing told a reader that the identifier is the patient rather than the provider, that it is minted per data source, or that a join to another PLIDA module has to go through the spine.
